the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

## Task fd6a563b: connect repeated colors in tiled grid

Solved successfully after one demo and two wrong submissions. This is the reusable pattern to check if a future task has the same setup.

### Visual structure
- A grid is a regular arrangement of rectangular/square tiles, separated by zero-valued gutters.
- Each tile has a uniform nonzero interior color and a border/frame of another color; tile interiors encode the color to connect.
- Output preserves the tiled grid and colors matching-color links in the empty gutters. It may also extend colored lines into the gutter-adjacent portions of a tile's frame, but never recolors the tile interior or overwrites its frame arbitrarily.

### Evidence from demonstrations
- Demo 1: 3x3 tiles with color-2 frame and a single center marker; same-colored center markers were linked horizontally/vertically through intervening zero gutters. Colors 1 and 3 got links; color 4 center markers did not.
- Demo 2: 4x4 tiles with color-3 frame and 2x2 interiors in colors 2/4/8. Repeated color-8 and color-4 interiors had links drawn through the gutters in aligned rows/columns. Other tile contents remained intact.
- Thus the general abstraction is matching interior colors, not matching tile frames. Think of all tiles as nodes on a grid and extend/link occurrences of a color along common rows or columns through the zero separator corridors. The particular generated layout can make links appear only in the gaps immediately adjoining same-color components, while other tile interiors remain unchanged.

### Verified test-specific output pattern
The solved 30x30 test had tile columns at x=1..5, 8..12, 15..19, 22..26, and tile-row bands y=1..5, 8..12, 16..20, 23..27 (0-based). Gutters are 2 cells wide, with variable 2/3-cell row gutters. Base frame color was 4; interior colors were 2, 3, or 8.

Correct output changes included:
- Top/bottom 3-color tile rows with interiors [3,2,2,3]: color 3 in the horizontal gutters adjacent to the endpoint 3 tiles (x=6,7 and x=13,14) along interior rows.
- Middle 8-color occurrences were linked in their aligned corridors; 3-color tiles likewise linked vertically/horizontally where the same interior color repeated.
- Gutters between matching colors were filled with that interior color; everything else remained as input.

### Strategy / cautions
1. Detect tile period from repeated frame/interior blocks and zero gutters; separate each tile's frame from its interior payload color.
2. Map each tile's interior color into a compact tile-level matrix; ignore the frame color as a connection color.
3. Find same-color tile payloads aligned in a row/column and fill the intervening zero gutter cells in the corresponding interior rows/columns with that payload color, following any observed endpoint-adjacent links. Preserve all nonzero tile pixels.
4. Carefully handle multiple interior rows/columns: links are made across the full payload thickness, not just a center pixel (demo 2 used 2-wide payloads; solved test used 3-wide payloads).
5. Do not assume all same colors link indiscriminately or fill across/over tile interiors. The demonstrated output only colors corridors and sometimes adjoining frame-edge positions; use exact alignment.
6. On ambiguous cases, one demonstration was highly informative; don’t waste submissions on speculative lines.

Note: these are observations from a single task family and one solved instance, not a universal ARC rule. Compare fresh task geometry and demos before applying.
